objective:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.

## What the seven measured arms show (Issue #125 forensics, 57,439 rows, width-20 beam)

Every number below is measured on the frozen checkpoints with the production evaluator.
"coverage" is the share of rows whose target SID survives among the twenty beams;
"alive" is the share whose gold prefix is still alive at that depth; acc@1 is the
teacher-forced top-1 accuracy of that position.

| arm | recall@10 | coverage | alive L1/L2/L3/L4 | acc@1 T1/T2/T3/T4 | distinct T1/T2/T3/T4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| resample | 0.06363 | 0.0884 | .497/.122/.091/.088 | .098/.152/**.794**/**.977** | 241/256/256/**10** |
| l1_only | 0.06233 | 0.0855 | 1.000/.829/.156/.086 | 1.000/.175/.106/.557 | 1/94/256/37 |
| l1_br_euclid | 0.06207 | 0.0847 | 1.000/.829/.161/.085 | 1.000/.178/.115/.550 | 1/80/256/44 |
| successor_geodesic_coarse | 0.05500 | 0.0740 | **.989**/.341/.122/.074 | .248/.180/.338/.737 | **26**/223/256/68 |
| tangent_successor_residual | 0.05500 | 0.0731 | .643/.180/.090/.073 | .121/.187/.527/**.885** | 238/251/256/**27** |
| successor_entropy | 0.05122 | 0.0688 | .735/.400/.133/.069 | .262/.338/.412/.680 | 250/211/256/91 |
| l1_br | 0.04671 | 0.0678 | 1.000/1.000/1.000/.068 | 1.000/1.000/1.000/.008 | 1/1/1/16462 |

**The measured rule.** Recall@10 is ordered by coverage and by nothing else, and coverage
is the *joint* survival of the four positions. Two ingredients exist, and no arm has both:

1. **A coarse first level is free.** `successor_geodesic_coarse` put 26 codes in T1 and its
   gold first token survived 98.9% of the time; but its loss moved to depth 2 (65% of the
   rows drop there) and its coverage only reached 0.0740.
2. **A decisive tail is what pays.** `resample` has the *worst* first-token survival of all
   arms (0.497, T1 acc 0.098) and still the best coverage, because its third token is
   correct 79.4% of the time given the oracle prefix and its fourth token 97.7% of the
   time, over a fourth-token alphabet of only ten values. `l1_br` is the same shape
   inverted: everything in T4 (16,462 values, 9.03 nats) and 93% of the rows drop at
   depth 4.

Extrapolating the measured per-level ratios, a first level as free as
`successor_geodesic_coarse` combined with the tail ratios of `resample` would give a
coverage near 0.17 instead of 0.088, i.e. roughly double the best arm.

## What this round must design

A mechanism whose **joint survival** is maximised: a first level that is cheap to predict
*and* behaviourally meaningful, plus a tail that is decisive. Concretely, the proposal
must aim for a first level of roughly 16-64 effective groups whose gold token survives
almost always, and for the later positions to be nearly determined by the earlier ones
(T3 top-1 around 0.7 or better, T4 nearly deterministic over a small extension alphabet),
while keeping a genuine behaviour-conditioned hyperbolic computation and a train-only
behaviour signal on one connected path.

The behaviour conditioning may act on the first-level assignment, on the residual path
that feeds T2/T3, or on both; what matters is that it *changes the curved computation*
that produces the tokens, and that the proposal states why the coupling makes the later
tokens more predictable rather than merely different. A mechanism that only renumbers the
first level, or that only pushes the information into T4, is out of scope.

A plain codebook-size change is out of scope; a curved assignment with no behaviour term
is out of scope.

Propose two or three ideas from *different* coupling sites, for example: a coarse hyperbolic
first level whose prototypes are placed by the train-only successor structure together with
a residual-level coupling; a curved assignment whose *second* level inherits the behaviour
prototype through the tangent transport; a hierarchical geometry where one behaviour
prototype steers the first level and the residual transport, so the third code becomes a
near-deterministic function of the first two.

Each idea must state its three arms (both-on, behaviour-off, geometry-off) and the predicted
direction of: `L1 Hard ER` on the canonical 52,855 pairs with ten fixed negatives,
gold-prefix survival at depths 1-4 under width-20 beam search, the teacher-forced NLL and
top-1 accuracy of T3 and T4, and Stage 3 `test_R@10` (target > 0.065).

## Frozen constraints

Four-token fixed-width SID with the deterministic collision-extension token, 3000 Stage 2
epochs on four cards, no early stopping, no test-time tuning, the frozen Stage 3 protocol,
and no validation or test behaviour in SID construction.
